topic: What orbital configurations justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication?
response: Orbital configurations with large buffer sizes and high data rates justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication. This is because V-band offers a higher data rate capacity, up to hundreds of Gbps, without the limitations of spectrum availability.
reference_context: The context highlights that optical links can outperform RF solutions if a reasonably sized buffer is available on board the satellite and high data rates are required. However, it also notes that RF systems are strongly spectrum-limited, making V-band a more suitable option for high-capacity applications.
